messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: High NotReady node count in infer-pool-usw (5 nodes showing kubelet restarts). Pager triggered. PagerDuty: @Alex you are oncall.
Alex: I'm seeing a spike in 504s for infer-usw production routes. dashboard shows CPU stable but node NotReady events ramping. starting triage.
Maria: attaching brief kernel/kubelet logs from one affected node: 
```
Mar 12 03:21:12 node-47 kubelet[1234]: E0312 03:21:12 kubelet.go:2509] node status not ready: kubelet restarted (reason: CrashLoop)
Mar 12 03:21:14 node-47 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 4123 (runtime-server) score 987 or sacrifice child
Mar 12 03:21:15 runtime: fatal error: runtime: out of memory
Mar 12 03:21:16 runtime-server: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS: cuCtxPushCurrent failed
```
Maria: looks like repeated OOMs + CUDA illegal address bubbles up after kubelet restart. Possibly stale nvml state after driver flip.
Sam: Confirmed: 5 nodes showed kubelet restart in last 6m. 3 of them had containers OOMKilled, 2 had docker/containerd crashes. Traffic fallback kicked to other regions but capacity saturated -> customer latency.
Alex: Impact estimate? how many requests 5xx?
Jen: From logs + metrics: about 7% of tokens produced in last 10m returned 5xx/timeout for infer-usw, error spike started at 03:20 UTC. Customer-facing errors: chat and completion endpoints for a handful of mid-size tenants.
Sam: Steps I'm executing: 1) Marking affected nodes unschedulable. 2) Evict non-daemon pods, let inference pods restart onto healthy nodes. 3) Temporarily increase fallback concurrency cap for rwa-traffic-router to accelerate failover.
Alex: runbook says try soft-restart kubelet only if node not recovering. do not drain GPUs until we confirm driver status.
Maria: Agreed. I'll attempt a graceful kubelet restart + nv-host restart on one node to validate. doing on node-47 now.
Alex: annotate service: "incident/2501234567" and attach. Jen, please open a customer-impact ticket and ping support with list of tenants affected.
Jen: on it — creating ticket and tagging #support-escalations.
Maria: node-47 after restart: kubelet came back but runtime-server pod OOMKilled again on boot. kernel shows repeated page allocation failures referencing cgroup.memory.limit_in_bytes. Looks like cgroup eviction thresh went low.
Sam: I'm temporarily increasing eviction hard limit on the node pool controller for infer-pool-usw to avoid immediate evictions while we scale. Also triggering scale-up of dedicated pool to absorb traffic.
Alex: Good. Any quick mitigation to keep customers alive? route policy to route non-critical traffic to infer-usw-fallback-model-lt which is CPU-backed (higher latency but more robust).
Sam: Done. Routed ~30% of baseline traffic. error rate down to ~2.1% now. latency up ~70ms for those requests.
Maria: Gathering additional logs, will try rolling driver reload sequence on a single node: unload nvidia, restart containerd, then start runtime. If successful, roll other nodes with pause between each.
Alex: We need an oncall handoff at 04:00 UTC. Who takes next shift? Sam: I can extend till 04:20 but need handoff to Jen afterwards. Jen: I can take 04:20-06:00.
incident-bot: Reminder: Incident channel created: #incident-2501234567, runbook: internal link.
Maria: Quick note for RCA: observed pattern -> kubelet restarts (why?) -> cgroup resets + container memory accounting inconsistent -> runtime OOMs -> CUDA illegal address on restart -> node NotReady. Suspect kernel-driver interaction or a noisy process on host causing mem pressure.
Sam: Action items captured: (1) full node memory profiling, (2) validate driver versions across pool, (3) add pre-drain health probe for GPU NVML state, (4) tweak autoscaler to prefer warm spare nodes.
Jen: Customer comms draft in support ticket: short apology, mitigation in place, ETA for full recovery 2h while we validate nodes and perform controlled roll.
Alex: Good. If we can confirm driver reload fixes one node, proceed with rolling across nodes with 30m pauses. Keep me updated, escalate if error rate >5% again. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Deploy request queued: autoscaler config change to increase warm pool by 2 nodes. awaiting approval.
Alex: Approved. Sam please proceed.
Sam: Approved and applied. monitor shows node count +2 warm nodes provisioning. error rate moving down to 0.9% over last 5m.
Jen: I'll update customers on status and ETA. Updating incident summary in #incident-2501234567.
Alex: Thanks team. Leaving a note: follow-up RCA to include memory cgroup behavior and potential guardrail to avoid container OOM cascades during kubelet restarts.
Jen: adding follow-up tickets and assigning to runtime team (Maria) and infra (Sam). closing active pager for now but keeping channel open for handoff notes.
Maria: I'll collect heap dumps/metrics and post in the incident channel.
Sam: Leaving monitoring alerts suppressed for this incident window to avoid noise.
incident-bot: Pager cleared for incident 2501234567 at 03:45 UTC (auto).
